topic: AWS Certified Data Engineer - Associate (DEA-C01) exam preparation - AWS's associate certification for designing, building, securing, and operating data pipelines and analytics solutions on AWS (Glue, Redshift, Kinesis, EMR, Athena, Lake Formation, and more)
exam_format: 65 questions (50 scored + 15 unscored), multiple choice and multiple response, 130 minutes, taken at a Pearson VUE test center or online-proctored. Scaled score 100-1000 with a passing score of 720. UNLIKE many vendors, AWS DOES publish official per-domain percentage weightings for DEA-C01, so this course uses the REAL published weights (not editorial estimates). Exam fee is USD 150 and varies by region; present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current AWS pricing.
question_types: multiple choice (one correct of four) and multiple response (two or more correct of five or more); scenario-based questions about designing and operating AWS data pipelines
audience: Data engineers, ETL developers, analytics engineers, and cloud practitioners who build and operate data pipelines on AWS. AWS recommends 2-3 years of data-engineering experience and 1-2 years of hands-on AWS. A strong complement to the AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer - Associate (MLA-C01) and AWS Solutions Architect Associate courses in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Data Ingestion and Transformation
domains.notes: The largest domain (OFFICIAL 34%). Ingesting data from streaming and batch sources: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and Firehose, Amazon MSK (Kafka), AWS DMS, AWS DataSync, and Amazon AppFlow. Transforming and processing with AWS Glue (jobs, crawlers, DynamicFrames, Glue Studio), Amazon EMR (Spark/Hive), AWS Lambda, and Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink. Orchestration with AWS Step Functions, Amazon MWAA (Airflow), and EventBridge. Handling data formats (Parquet, ORC, Avro, JSON), partitioning, compression, and schema evolution. Choosing the correct ingestion and transformation service and pattern for a described throughput, latency, and cost requirement.

domains.name: Data Store Management
domains.notes: Choosing and modeling the right store (OFFICIAL 26%): Amazon S3 and S3 storage classes / lifecycle / Intelligent-Tiering, building a data lake with AWS Lake Formation and the Glue Data Catalog, and querying with Amazon Athena. Data warehousing with Amazon Redshift (distribution/sort keys, RA3, Redshift Spectrum, Serverless). Operational stores: Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon RDS/Aurora, and when to use each. Cataloging, schema discovery, and metadata management. Selecting the correct storage/warehouse/catalog design for a described access pattern, scale, and cost.

domains.name: Data Operations and Support
domains.notes: Operating pipelines in production (OFFICIAL 22%): automating with Lambda/Step Functions/EventBridge, monitoring and logging with Amazon CloudWatch (metrics, logs, alarms) and AWS CloudTrail, and troubleshooting failed jobs and data-quality issues (Glue Data Quality, Deequ patterns). Optimizing performance and cost of Glue, EMR, Redshift, and Athena. Ensuring data pipeline reliability, retries, idempotency, and SLAs; analyzing data with Athena/Redshift and visualizing with Amazon QuickSight at an awareness level. Choosing the correct operational, monitoring, or optimization action for a described production problem.

domains.name: Data Security and Governance
domains.notes: Securing and governing data (OFFICIAL 18%): encryption at rest and in transit with AWS KMS, S3 encryption, and TLS; access control with IAM policies, roles, Lake Formation permissions, and fine-grained (row/column) access. Data privacy, masking, and PII handling; auditing with CloudTrail; and governance with the Glue Data Catalog and Lake Formation. VPC endpoints, network isolation, and secrets management (AWS Secrets Manager). Choosing the correct security, encryption, access-control, or governance control for a described compliance or least-privilege requirement.

extra_guidance: AWS Certified Data Engineer - Associate (DEA-C01) is AWS's data-engineering associate certification and a hot, high-demand credential that complements the AWS Machine Learning Engineer - Associate (MLA-C01) and Solutions Architect Associate courses already in this catalog. IMPORTANT and DIFFERENT from the NVIDIA/Google courses: AWS DOES publish official per-domain percentage weightings, so this course uses the REAL published weights - Data Ingestion and Transformation 34%, Data Store Management 26%, Data Operations and Support 22%, Data Security and Governance 18% - present these as AWS's OFFICIAL weightings (no leading '~', no 'editorial estimate' disclaimer), because they are official. The passing score is a scaled 720/1000, which IS official and may be stated. This is a service-selection and scenario exam: the real skill is choosing the RIGHT AWS service and pattern for a described data-pipeline requirement, so practice questions MUST be scenario-based with 'MOST cost-effective / LEAST operational overhead / BEST performance' framing (classic AWS style) and MUST use exact AWS service names and features. Cover the classic decision pairs relentlessly: Kinesis Data Streams vs Firehose vs MSK; Glue ETL vs EMR vs Lambda; Redshift vs Athena vs EMR for query; S3 storage classes and lifecycle; DynamoDB vs RDS/Aurora; Step Functions vs MWAA for orchestration; Lake Formation fine-grained access vs IAM; KMS encryption choices. Anchor everything to real AWS service behavior and quotas; do NOT invent limits. Labs are read-and-understand AWS walkthroughs (build a Glue job + crawler, stream with Kinesis Firehose to S3, query a data lake with Athena, load Redshift, set Lake Formation permissions, add KMS encryption), not deep coding. Frame the credential honestly as 'exam-focused preparation' - never promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in any form (Udemy compliance). Final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a time-management strategy for the 65-question, 130-minute format and guidance on multiple-response elimination. Present the exam fee as approximate (USD 150) and advise verifying current AWS pricing. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor terms (Azure/GCP) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
